models.note: A general-purpose SD1.5 model. Trained at 512 and expects the full text encoder.
An SDXL model. Trained at 1024 and falls apart when asked for much less.
An anime model in the NovelAI lineage, trained so that skipping the last text-encoder layer is the intended setting.

scenes.label: A person
scenes.prompt: a lighthouse keeper standing on a cliffside path at golden hour, facing the viewer, weathered kindly face, coastal village below, dramatic sky, sweeping ocean view, cinematic lighting, highly detailed

scenes.label: A place
scenes.prompt: a cliffside path winding down to a coastal village at golden hour, whitewashed cottages, harbour wall and moored fishing boats, dramatic sky, sweeping ocean view, cinematic lighting, highly detailed
scenes.derived_from: The txt2img tutorial prompt with the keeper removed, so the same world is shown without a face to judge

scenes.label: A thing
scenes.prompt: a lighthouse keeper's brass lantern on a weathered wooden table, salt-stained glass, coiled rope and a folded chart beside it, golden hour light through a window, cinematic lighting, highly detailed
scenes.derived_from: The txt2img tutorial prompt reduced to one object, so texture-led parameters have something small to act on

sweeps.rationale: SD1.5 and SDXL settle at different step counts, so both baselines are shown; the anime model behaves like SD1.5 here and would only repeat it.
sweeps.caption: How many denoising steps the sampler takes. More steps cost more time, and stop helping well before they stop costing.

stops.caption: Too few steps to resolve the scene: shapes are blocky and colour smears.
The composition arrives, but edges and faces are still soft.
Detail starts to settle and small features become readable.
Close to this model's best for the scene; most of what you will get is here.
The common default. Extra steps now mostly refine texture.
Little you can see over 30, for well over twice the time and kudos.

sweeps.rationale: SDXL burns out at a lower guidance than SD1.5, so the two baselines diverge; the anime model tracks SD1.5 closely enough that a third strip teaches nothing new.
sweeps.caption: How hard the model is pushed to follow your prompt. Too low and it ignores you; too high and it overcooks the image.

stops.caption: The model barely listens to your prompt: washed out and generic.
Loose adherence and soft colour, with room for the model's own ideas.
A gentle balance, good when your prompt is already detailed.
The usual home base for most models.
Firmer adherence, with contrast and saturation starting to climb.
Overcooked: harsh contrast, burnt colour and crunchy edges.

sweeps.rationale: Ancestral and converging samplers separate differently on each baseline, so one photoreal SD1.5 model and one SDXL model cover the contrast at fixed steps.
sweeps.caption: Which algorithm walks the image out of noise. At the same steps and seed, each one lands somewhere slightly different.

stops.caption: Fast and predictable, and a good baseline to compare the others against.
Ancestral: it adds fresh noise each step, so the image keeps changing as you add steps.
Converges quickly and is often the cleanest result at 20 to 30 steps.
Stochastic, so it lands somewhere of its own, often with richer texture.

sweeps.rationale: All three models, because the comparison is the lesson: 2 is right for the anime-lineage model and wrong for the other two.
sweeps.caption: How many layers to cut from the end of the text encoder. Anime-lineage models were trained expecting one to be cut.

stops.caption: The full text encoder. What most non-anime models expect.
Skips the last layer. On an anime-lineage model this is the intended setting; elsewhere it just loosens the prompt.
Skipping further loses prompt detail, and your wording starts to be ignored.

sweeps.rationale: The failure hires-fix repairs only appears above a model's native size, so the strip must render above it; at native size the flag does nothing at all. SD1.5 shows it at 2x native (1024), where the doubling artifacts are unmistakable.
sweeps.caption: Above a model's native size, one pass repeats what it knows. Hires-fix generates small first, then enlarges and refines.

stops.caption: One pass at the full size. Above what the model knows you get duplicated details and stretched shapes.
Generated small, then enlarged and re-diffused, so the composition stays coherent.

sweeps.rationale: SDXL degrades more gently past native, so 1.5x (1536) is enough to show the repair without an extreme render.
sweeps.caption: Above a model's native size, one pass repeats what it knows. Hires-fix generates small first, then enlarges and refines.

stops.caption: One pass at the full size. Above what the model knows you get duplicated details and stretched shapes.
Generated small, then enlarged and re-diffused, so the composition stays coherent.

sweeps.rationale: Seam behaviour is a sampler-level effect that reads the same on every baseline, so one model is enough; shown on the object scene, which is what anyone actually tiles.
sweeps.caption: Whether the edges are made to wrap. Shown repeated four times, because that is the only way you can see it.

stops.caption: Edges end wherever they like, so repeating the image shows hard seams.
Edges are made to wrap, so the image repeats seamlessly as a texture.

sweeps.rationale: SDXL only, because the degradation being taught is SDXL-specific: it is what happens when you ask an SDXL model for the sizes an SD1.5 model was built for.
sweeps.caption: Every model has a size it was trained at. Ask an SDXL model for much less and it does not simply get smaller, it gets worse.

stops.caption: Far below anything SDXL saw in training: the image collapses into mush.
Still far too small. Shapes appear, but nothing holds together.
Native for SD1.5, and still wrong here: anatomy and framing come out muddled.
SDXL's native size. This is what the model was trained to make.

sweeps.rationale: One grid per baseline, because steps and guidance interact differently for SD1.5, for SDXL, and for the anime lineage.
sweeps.caption: Steps and guidance are not independent. Read across for guidance and down for steps: both have to be in range before an image looks right.
